MOVE below 80 is calm, 80-120 is moderate uncertainty, and 150+ is high stress; 106.84 is moderate. SOFR measures secured overnight funding, not unsecured bank funding. NFCI below zero indicates looser-than-average broad financial conditions; -0.496 is the weekly observation for Oct 16, not a live reading. It rose 0.006 from the prior weekly row but remains negative.

Fed & Policy Watch
  • The Federal Reserve Board calendar lists the October 27-28 FOMC meeting event on Wednesday Oct 28 at 2:00 PM ET and the press conference at 2:30 PM ET; both are High-impact scheduled catalysts.
  • Selected Board statistical releases, checked against each item's own day list: H.8 Fri Oct 23 and Fri Oct 30 at 4:15 PM; H.10 Mon Oct 26 at 4:15 PM; H.6 Tue Oct 27 at 1:00 PM; H.4.1 Thu Oct 29 at 4:30 PM. Routine CP and H.15 rows are omitted.
  • BEA's publisher schedule lists third-quarter advance GDP Thu Oct 29 at 8:30 AM ET. BEA schedules September Personal Income and Outlays for Nov 4 at 8:30 AM; the New York Fed October calendar instead lists Personal Income and the PCE Deflator Oct 29 at 8:30 AM. This material date conflict is unresolved; both publisher dates are displayed separately.
  • Chicago Fed's next scheduled NFCI release is Oct 28 for the week ending Oct 23. The latest observed NFCI in the returned data is -0.496 for the week ending Oct 16.
Omissions and Watch
  • Calendar completeness is limited to the selected checked sources. No remaining scheduled events were elapsed at the 00:30:36 ET cutoff. CPI, PPI, Employment Situation, Retail Sales and GDP/PCE are distinct releases; no CPI, PPI, Employment Situation or Retail Sales release is scheduled in Oct 23-30 in the checked New York Fed calendar. The November New York Fed calendar lists CPI Nov 10 and PPI Nov 13; they are outside this week-ahead window.
  • Conflict/cleanup check: the New York Fed October calendar and Census agree on Durable Goods and New Residential Sales Oct 27; Census also lists the Advance Economic Indicators Report and third-quarter Housing Vacancies Oct 28. Chicago Fed dates CFSEC on Oct 22, not today, and its Oct 28 NFCI release is for the week ending Oct 23. The NY Fed lists WEI on Oct 22 and again Oct 29, not today; elapsed events are not carried forward. Dallas Fed says the Texas Retail Outlook Survey has not been published since January 2026, so the stale Oct 27 NY Fed entry for that survey is omitted. Chicago CFNAI is verified for Oct 26, September 2026.
  • Primary sources checked: New York Fed October and November Economic Indicators Calendars; Federal Reserve Board October calendar and H.4.1 page; Census 2026 calendar; BEA release schedule; Chicago Fed release calendar and NFCI file; TreasuryDirect auction data; University of Michigan; Conference Board; Dallas Fed WEI and survey schedules; Philadelphia Fed page; EIA petroleum and natural-gas schedules; and Treasury yield data. BLS.gov was not requested; BLS timing is sourced from the New York Fed calendar. The Richmond Fed page request was refused, so its Oct 27 survey date/time is cited to the New York Fed's date-specific calendar only.
  • EIA petroleum and natural-gas schedule pages did not provide a verified date-specific release in Oct 23-30; no weekly release is projected from cadence. WTI is a material market watch at $99.96, up 0.49% from Thursday's prior daily bar. Monitor energy-price sensitivity without inferring an EIA release time. The University of Michigan's October survey page reports year-ahead inflation expectations of 4.7% and long-run expectations of 3.5%, and notes the post-Iran-conflict comparison; this is an official survey finding, not a new geopolitical alert. No separately verified unscheduled policy or geopolitical alert from this run.
  • No exchange-specific market-structure event or product-hours review was verified. Confirm contract month, exchange hours, liquidity and event updates before execution. Selected-calendar omissions include routine Fed CP/H.15 releases and other non-key regional/statistical rows.
Trading Strategy Note | ES Futures
BASE CASE
Treat the 12:20 AM ET ES=F quote as overnight context only: the generic continuous quote is not a contract-bound execution reference and the current daily bar is in progress. SPY's Thursday close fell, while VIX and MOVE rose; MOVE at 106.84 remains in the moderate-uncertainty band. Today's 10:00 AM Michigan final survey is the next listed catalyst; the Oct 28 FOMC decision/press conference, Oct 29 advance GDP and disputed PCE timing are important checkpoints. Use live yields, volatility and market depth to assess price discovery; this is a scenario framework, not a directional forecast or trade signal.
INVALIDATION
Reassess if ES sustains a range break without confirmation from live Treasury yields, volatility and market depth, or if the selected contract's hours differ. No unsupported levels or targets are supplied; reconfirm live quotes, scheduled-event updates and contract details before execution.
